output.review_comment:
Two of the fixes are good: the off-by-one correction (`top - first + 1` for inclusive tiers) and the `ValueError` for negative quantities both match the docstring.

The problem is the new "volume pricing" branch. Once the quantity reaches the open-ended tier, it charges every unit at that tier's rate. The PR description says this was added only so `test_bulk_order` passes, that no documentation describes it, and that it contradicts the docstring's graduated pricing: the docstring gives 120,000 cents for 600 units, but this code returns 90,000. The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth, so this branch is the wrong fix. It also changes prices for every order that reaches the top tier, not just the tested one, and it creates a jump in pricing: 499 units would cost more than 600.

Please remove the open-ended-tier early return and keep plain graduated pricing. `top = quantity if last is None else min(quantity, last)` still works once the +1 fix is in. If `test_bulk_order` really conflicts with the docstring, don't make the code match the test. Leave that test failing and raise the conflict with the teammate, so they can decide whether the test or the spec is wrong.
